# PEN-4932 — provision the per-agent workspace claim (stage 4b, provisioner only)

Tracking: [PEN-4932](https://paperclip.blockcast.net/PEN/issues/PEN-4932) · PR: [#3168](https://github.com/Blockcast/paperclip/pull/3168)

## 1. Initial change

**Files:** `src/server/workspace-pvc.ts`, `src/server/workspace-pvc.test.ts`, `src/server/k8s-client.ts`, `src/server/k8s-client-pvc.test.ts`

Adds `ensureAgentWorkspacePvc` and the two Core API helpers it needs (`getPvc`, `createPvc`), which this adapter did not have. **Nothing calls it.** It is the provisioning half of stage 4b, landed reviewed and inert ahead of the `dataClaimName` swap — the same posture #3153/#3157/#3158 took for the prompt-bundle delivery channel, and for the same reason: the swap is the first change in this issue that is not inert, so the pieces it composes are better reviewed one at a time than inside it.

**Why the claim is `ReadWriteMany`, when the in-tree per-agent precedent is `ReadWriteOnce`.** `opencode-db-<agentId>` (`paperclip.io/pvc-type=agent-db`) is the pattern this follows for naming, labels and the get-then-create shape, but **its access mode must not be copied**. One agent runs up to `maxConcurrentRuns` Job pods at once and the scheduler does not co-locate them — measured 2026-10-28 in namespace `paperclip`, agent `29033747` held pods on `k8s-paperclip-3` (x2), `-7` and `-11` simultaneously. An RWO claim there hits `Multi-Attach` and wedges every concurrent run of that agent, which is strictly worse and far more frequent than the node-wide blast radius PEN-4932 exists to reduce. The opencode claim gets away with RWO because exactly one opencode process uses each. RWX costs nothing against the objective: each dynamically provisioned CephFS PVC gets its own subvolume and its own `volumeHandle` regardless of access mode, and ceph-csi's `IDLocker` keys on that Volume ID — **distinctness, not exclusivity, is what buys the smaller blast radius.** This is pinned by a test rather than left to the next reader to re-derive, precisely because the nearest precedent in this tree says the opposite.

**Capacity is derived, not picked.** `50Gi`. A per-agent claim does not carry only agent-scoped data: the company-scoped trees (project checkout, `wt/<companyId>`, the pnpm store, `work/<companyId>`) are read by every agent of the same company, so per-agent volumes duplicate them. Plan §5 measures that at ≈13.2 G per company; corroborated independently 2026-10-30 from a live agent pod (`projects` 4.9 G, pnpm store 3.0 G, `run-logs` 399 K). `50Gi` is ~4x the measured steady state. It is a ceiling and not an allocation — CephFS subvolume quotas are thin provisioned — and not a one-way door, since the `cephfs` class sets `allowVolumeExpansion: true`. The default StorageClass `cephfs` was read off the live cluster rather than assumed, because the design needs a class that can dynamically provision RWX; `paperclip-data` itself is `cephfs.csi.ceph.com`, RWX, `Delete`, expansion enabled.

**A 409 on create is success; nothing else is.** Two concurrent runs of the same agent can both observe "absent" and both create. The loser must not fail its run — the winner created exactly the object this call wanted, under a name that encodes the agent id, so there is no ambiguity about whose claim it is. The tolerance is deliberately narrow: a 403 (RBAC) propagates, because returning a claim name nothing provisioned would strand the Job on a volume that does not exist and report the wrong fault. RBAC is already in place — the chart's Role grants `create`/`delete`/`get` on `persistentvolumeclaims` for the opencode per-agent claims — so this adds no chart change.

**`getPvc` does not reuse `execute.ts`'s `isK8s404`, and that is the one non-obvious call here.** That predicate checks `response.statusCode`, `response.status` and `statusCode`, but **not `code`** — which is the only field @kubernetes/client-node actually sets. `ApiException` is built as `super("HTTP-Code: " + code + ...)` and then assigns only `this.code`, so `isK8s404` works today purely on its message regex; `isK8s409` documents exactly this asymmetry in its own header and checks `code` for that reason. For a get-then-create the gap is not cosmetic: a missed 404 turns "this claim does not exist yet" into a thrown error that fails the run instead of provisioning the volume it was about to mount. The local predicate checks `code` as well. `isK8s404` is left alone — widening it is a change to a path this PR does not exercise, and it is reachable from the run path.

The 409/404 tests use a fixture shaped like a real `ApiException` (both `code` and a matching message), which on its own **cannot distinguish the `code` check from the message regex** — it passes either way. A second fixture carries the status only as a structured field under an opaque message; that is the assertion the regex cannot satisfy. Mutation-checked: dropping `|| e.code === 404` turns exactly that one test red, and flipping the access mode to `ReadWriteOnce` turns exactly the RWX test red.

`agentWorkspaceClaimName` is pure and exported so the manifest builder and the provisioner derive the name identically — two places computing a claim name independently is how a Job ends up mounting a claim nothing provisioned. It throws on an id with no DNS-1123 characters rather than returning the bare `agent-workspace-` prefix, which would be the same name for every such id and would silently give two agents one claim.

**What this does NOT do, and must not be read as doing:** it does not change `dataClaimName`, so every agent pod still mounts `paperclip-data` and the measured blast radius is unchanged. The claim cannot be adopted until the prompt bundle reaches the pod over a channel that does not assume a shared volume (invariant 1) — on a per-agent claim the server writes a complete bundle into its own volume and the pod gets the seeded, empty directory, so `--append-system-prompt-file` names a file that does not exist and the agent silently loses its instructions. Adoption also requires #3165's split seeder shape on `master` first: `resolveSeedShape` picks `split` for a non-self claim, and seeding a per-agent claim with the `self-claim` shape even once leaves root-owned intermediates that `split` can never create inside afterwards.

Suite: 31 files / 1861 tests green, `tsc --noEmit` clean.
